report.answer_text:
The Vera C. Rubin Observatory’s June 23, 2025 “First Look” showed the Trifid and Lagoon nebulae, two stellar nurseries in the Milky Way, in striking detail. It also revealed a wide view of the Virgo Cluster region, with about 10 million galaxies visible across the full panorama. The same test observations uncovered more than 2,100 previously unknown asteroids. (rubinobservatory.org)
Rubin is carrying out the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), a 10-year survey that began in late June 2026. It images the southern sky every few nights to build a time-lapse record that will help astronomers track asteroids, catch events such as supernovae, map the Milky Way, and study dark matter and dark energy. (rubinobservatory.org)
